@ak_dfranco No directional opinion yet on $NOK since I don’t know enough about the company.

But definitely taking a look after $NVDA took a stake.

I've been the first few to cover many supply chain photonic names.

Most are up 100-400%+ since I've posted.

Here's the TLDR overview of my thesis posts:

“Safest” Longs as of Today:

- $TSEM (Tower Semi)
- $SOI (Soitec)
- $COHR - Defensible compounders over time. 

Soitec - Substrate monopoly over silicon photonics / CPO architectural ramp at dirt cheap valuation (after recent 40%+ rise maybe still 1.4x book)

Tower Semi - P/E in the 10's for 2028, 70%+ capacity booked already, $NVDA architectural partner, and basically the pure play $TSM of photonics. 

Coherent - Basically does everything from materials/substrates to lasers to transceivers in photonics. As well as fundamental supplier to many other verticals. 

Most High Beta/Extreme Growth Longs:

$AXTI  - InP duopoly with Sumitomo (that getting export controlled), upstream feedstock duopoly with Vital. 

Basically at the top of the entire photonics food chain is AXT. There's certainty export control risks, but my thesis is that if AXT goes down, the photonic buildout with AI goes down. So might as well go long on AXT. 

$AAOI - 10x revenue ramp into 2027. Laser -> Design -> Assembly, Made in America. Main uncertainty is execution, scaling laser capacity that they've bought from $COHR, etc. 

Demand from hyperscalers are all there. Can they deliver? I'd take the risk.

$IQE - Basically completely dependent on restructuring and clearing debt (~$200M MC). Known $LITE supplier for epiwafers, and their main competitor was Landmark with a $3.5B+ valuation.  

The latent capacity is there with reactors, but they basically need to pull off a successful pivot over to photonics and cut off legacy drag for 10x rerating. 

Highest risk out there, but maybe worth the reward.s 

Long $GOOGL TPU Ecosystem:

$LITE - Basically very high BOM related to optical due to OCS monopoly for Google. 

If you think Google TPU is a trillion dollar program that might end up like $NVDA, go long on $LITE. 

Google has $175-180B capex planned for 2026, and their CTO for AI Infra said they plan to up that Y/Y, probably spending $1 trillion in the next 8 years. 

If that holds up, $LITE is extremely undervalued relative to forward potential. Of course the supply lasers to other hyperscalers too, but I'd say it's more heavily tethered to Google growth. 

_

There's a ton of others out there I've covered like:

$POET - I'm personally not long, but $400M balance sheet gives it good cushion. Just found Celestial from $MRVL ramp was too far out, eg. $500 million 2028, $1 billion 2029 projections, for revenue to be too material as of 2026. 

It largely depends if their interposers get other hyperscaler qualifications rather than backdooring through Marvell, which was the main bull case. 

$HIMX- I did find this thesis to be slightly compelling as a likely $TSM COUPE supplier. 

But personally, I preferred $SOI, and would just put more concentration into that (since Soitec known supplier already to basically everything silicon photonics, and is just coming out of a downturn). 

There’s a lot more like $NOK, $SHMN, that are interesting, but I’ve personally out concentration into the ones I find most compelling.

As “crowded names” like $LITE, it does not mean there’s no upside left. It just happens to be more priced in until there’s new news.

There's a lot of "critical suppliers" but there's a difference between importance in the supply chain...

And converting that into extreme revenue growth eg. $AAOI -> $4.5 billion in revenue. 

But for TLDR photonics exposure, my portfolio looks similar to this:

High Concentration (Safer)
$TSEM foundry, $SOI substrate, $COHR everything

Mix of Long + CSP (High Volaility):
$AXTI substrate/feedstock, $IQE epiwafer, $AAOI transceiver supply chain

TLDR from analyst note: The AI infrastructure investment supercycle follows a strict "bottleneck resolution" sequence: 

Compute/GPUs (2023) -> Memory/HBM (2024) ->  Interconnect/Networking (2025+).

Translation:

 "We judge that the third investment cycle of the AI value chain has officially begun. Following GPUs (2023) and HBM (2024), post-2025, optical interconnects will become the fastest-growing core segment. 

2027–2028 will be a critical inflection point where CPO commercialization. 1.6T standardization, and Scale-Up optical transitions align, structurally expanding the TAM of related industries"

Some takeaways:
1. CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) is moving from the lab to commercial mass production
2. 2027-2028 is the major structural inflection point (good idea to frontrun this now in 2026 from testing with $AEHR to ELS with $SIVE or packaging with $POET). 
3. The Total Addressable Market (TAM) for optical components, materials, and testing equipment is expected to structurally expand 3x to 5x (I think this is sandbagging a bit).

$NOK just reported Q2 earnings.

A bunch of people were aping into $NOK earnings and have no clue what to think now the print is out...

Especially since markets are closed so no reaction and this isn't a business where top line revenue growth is what investors are watching. 

At first glance these are mid. Reported operating loss of €50M, $0 EPS, negative €732M fcf, no operational raise...

But what we really care about is that $NOK AI & Cloud revenue grew 105% last quarter while the telecom business grew 4%.

AI and Cloud did €446M in Q2, up from €220M a year ago. Now roughly 9% of group revenue. Sequentially it's up 29% quarter over quarter. So yeah roughly $1/$10 Nokia receives now comes from AI, which is pretty meaningful given it was around 4% last year and the thesis is that this becomes a larger and larger share over time.

Great to see optical is now 18% of group revenue. @AsymmetricBets_  May base case assumed 15%. Our sensitivity said every +5ppt of optical mix adds about 0.39x to the blended multiple, so 18% puts SOTP near 3.90x and roughly $17.20 against our $16.31 base.

What's most striking is the orders. €2.8B of AI & Cloud orders in a single quarter. Q1 was €1B so we're talking about cloud orders tripling in a single quarter. 

This is a business running at a €1.8B run rate and just booked €2.8B in three months so I expect the market to like this. Management says roughly half of those orders converts to revenue inside twelve months. So yes AI is going to becoming a MUCH bigger share of $NOK's business.

We already knew about San Jose ramping Q4 and Pennsylvania packaging going up 10x. Arizona is new. Nokia is buying NXP's chip plant in Chandler and converting it to InP. Definitley a shortcut to more production inheriting the cleanroom, power, permits etc. Basically says that management thinks the InP bottleneck lasts long term and their putting in the capex to meet it.

More to learn on the call. But curious to see if the market cares more about AI progress or headline misses.

Their Photonics-SOI substrate sits underneath basically every silicon photonics chip on earth, from TSMC's COUPE platform to the transceivers at $AAOI and $COHR to the CPO switches Nvidia and Broadcom are racing toward. They have 95%+ share.

So when photonics volumes move ($15B to $145B TAM per Goldman), Soitec is the first domino which is why Photonics-SOI sales doubled YoY and now make up more than half of the €65M Edge & Cloud AI segment. 

Total revenue hit €113M, up 23% at constant currency against guidance of 15%. Then they guided Q2 to 30%+ growth when the street was sitting at 4% which is awesome.

Unlike $NOK on their recent earnings, Soitec is showing that it actually has the capacity to execute. They qualified the Singapore 300mm fab for high volume production ahead of schedule, so now there's two qualified sites while sales are doubling, and they've got 10+ photonics customers signing multi-year capacity reservations with actual cash deposits attached. 

Make fun of bottleneck talk all you want but customers are prepaying a wafer supplier to lock supply beyond 2027. 

The CEO also confirmed the architecture point I flagged at GTC. Pluggables, NPO, and CPO all consume the same substrate, and CPO consumes multiples more wafer area per port. Soitec doesn't need to pick the winning architecture, but of course there is even more convexity when CPO does ramp providing a nice acceleration on top of what is already a rosy growth story.

Parts that weren't as bullish 

- Fab loading came in at 48% versus 74% a year ago
- €30M less government funding this year as IPCEI-II winds down.
- Mobile inventory still hasn't fully cleared, so margins lag the headline growth for a while.
- No H1 print until November, so this trades on tone for four months.

If you're still long Soitec, this company is doing everything it's supposed to, despite the large drawdown, and is still one of the biggest, most important chokepoints in the AI buildout. Morgan Stanley just went overweight the name with a €200 price target.

I am long $PENG, Penguin Solutions. 

After the drawdown, it sits 33% off its all-time high, an opportunity that’s hard to pass up.

Penguin doesn’t make the accelerator and doesn’t make the DRAM. It takes raw memory from manufacturers and packages it into custom modules built to spec, then stands up the clusters those modules go into. Whoever wins the socket, whoever wins the model, the boxes still get built and the memory still gets integrated.

This is why I like this company so much:

The memory business is not a segment anymore; IT IS THE COMPANY. Integrated Memory did $275 million last quarter and more than doubled year over year. That is 57% of a business that printed record net sales of $479 million, up 48%. GAAP operating income of $51 million, up 417%. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.68 against a one cent loss a year ago. Management raised full year guidance on both sales and EPS off the back of it.

Advanced Compute looks flat, $137.6 million against $132.5 million. The non-hyperscale piece, enterprise and sovereign and neoclouds, grew 81% year over year and is now 60% of that segment. The flat line is a deliberate pivot out of low margin hyperscaler work. The mix shift is hiding the growth. Hyperscalers build in house and always will. Everyone below them cannot, and there are more of them every quarter.

They have already proven they can execute at sovereign scale. The Haein cluster with SK Telecom, over 1,000 Blackwell GPUs, 50-plus miles of precision-laid fiber, integrated into SK Broadband’s Gasan data center. Order placement to go-live in two months. That is one of the fastest deployments of an AI supercomputing system at that scale that anyone has done.

Management is getting a serious upgrade. Mark Papermaster, the sitting CTO of AMD. Penny Herscher, who also chairs Lumentum. And now David Heard, who ran Infinera before Nokia bought it and who now leads Nokia’s Network Infrastructure division. Memory, CPU and photonics all sitting at the same nine person table.

The photonics leg is the optionality we get almost for free. Penguin called photonics early and was in Celestial AI before Marvell bought it. They are now building the Photonic Memory Appliance, a box that uses light to link memory across servers so an entire cluster shares one pool like it is one machine. IF it works it is the highest margin and most defensible IP in the company and nothing in the multiple reflects it. If it slips I still own a profitable memory and integration business.

The risks are here as with any growth stock

The cluster business is lumpy and one customer sliding a quarter wrecks the print. It already happened. Q2 was down 42% year over year. 

Cash conversion is thin. $11 million of operating cash flow year to date against record earnings, carried by a payables build. Record profit and weak cash in the same quarter is a thing I watch closely.

Part of Q3 net income came from equity investment disposals. Operating income was $51 million and net income landed at $44.7 million. Clean until you look at the mix.

High DRAM prices cut both ways. Great for the memory segment, and they also slow customer orders and squeeze gross margin.

Their photonics angle is a 2027 story. If it slips this sits dead money for a while.

The memory business is compounding right now, the growth in Advanced Compute is real and buried under a mix shift, they have already delivered a sovereign cluster in two months, and the board is built for a company three sizes larger than the one the market is pricing.

Execution is everything from here. 

Sovereign and enterprise AI spending has not ramped yet, and that spend is less cyclical than hyperscaler capex, which may peak in 2028.
